scenes.title: Who Feels Pity
scenes.summary: Pity is pain at an apparent evil, destructive or painful, befalling one who does not deserve it, such as one might expect to suffer oneself or one of one's own; so the utterly ruined and the very prosperous do not feel it, while the old, the weak, the educated and those with families do.

scenes.title: What Is Pitiable
scenes.summary: Pitiable are deaths, injuries, old age, disease and want, and the evils of fortune: friendlessness, ugliness, weakness, and good coming too late, as the king's gifts were sent down to Diopeithes after his death.

scenes.title: Whom People Pity
scenes.summary: People pity those they know, unless they are too close, as the son of Amasis wept for his friend begging but not for his son led to death, for the terrible drives out pity; they pity their like, and sufferings that seem near, which is why gestures, voice and dress make speakers more pitiable.
